candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls untrusted HTML/CSS, including the URI in an @import rule inside an allowed <style> element. The URL can name an arbitrary HTTP(S) host, including loopback, link-local, and internal addresses, provided it matches the policy URL regex.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The feature is explicitly opt-in and every bundled policy sets embedStyleSheets=false. CssHandler rejects relative imports and applies onsite/offsite URL regexes, and HttpGet does not inherit the caller's cookies. Those controls reduce exposure but do not enforce a host/IP allowlist or otherwise prevent requests to internal HTTP endpoints. The response is parsed rather than reflected, so this is primarily blind SSRF.
candidates.impact: Blind SSRF: the application server can be induced to issue requests to internal services or cloud metadata endpoints and can be used for internal reachability probing. The response is read into memory before the size check, so an oversized or slow response can also consume resources. Responses are parsed as CSS and not directly returned, and cookie management is disabled, which limits but does not eliminate the SSRF impact.
candidates.prerequisites: The caller sanitizes attacker-controlled HTML/CSS with a policy that sets embedStyleSheets=true and permits the <style> tag. All bundled policies set embedStyleSheets=false, so default-policy users are not exposed. The import must be absolute and match the broad onsite/offsite URL expressions.
candidates.root_cause: CssHandler.importStyle trusts an @import URI supplied in untrusted CSS and validates only whether it matches broad onsite/offsite URL regular expressions. CssScanner then creates an HttpGet directly from that URI and executes it server-side without restricting hosts, IP ranges, or resolving and re-checking the destination.
candidates.title: Server-side request forgery via attacker-controlled CSS @import when stylesheet embedding is enabled
candidates.trace: AntiSamy scan reaches the CSS scanner for a <style> element; CssScanner.scanStyleSheet calls getCleanStylesheetWithImports when shouldParseImportedStylesheets is true. CssHandler.importStyle receives the parser-provided URI, applies only URL-pattern validation, and enqueues it. parseImportedStylesheets removes the URI from the queue, constructs HttpGet(stylesheetUri), and calls httpClient.execute(stylesheetRequest), causing a server-originated request to the attacker-selected destination.
candidates.unverified: No policy/CSS payload was executed and no network request was made. Runtime confirmation is absent for the exact Batik parser callback behavior and regex acceptance under a custom policy. The HttpClient redirect policy and response-reading behavior were not tested in this environment.

coverage_summary: Reviewed the visible 54-file source scope, focusing on public scan entry points, DOM/SAX sanitization, CSS parsing/validation and URL handling, policy loading, serializers, entity handling, and the main bundled policy rules. The P1 index covers 48 of 54 source files, with 6 files missing from the index; it provides syntax/navigation candidates only, without control/data-flow or semantic resolution. No tests or build execution were available or used.
limitations: All bundled policies disable embedStyleSheets, so the submitted SSRF lead requires a non-default policy and does not affect default-policy deployments.
No runtime execution, payload testing, dependency-source inspection, or network activity was performed; reachability and parser behavior were inferred from source only.
The relation index omits 6 source files and does not implement data flow, semantic resolution, runtime reachability, or exploitability analysis.
The repository snapshot contains no visible test suite and no antisamy.xsd resource, limiting policy-loading verification.
Not every CSS property, every sample policy tag rule, or every third-party parser/serializer implementation detail was exhaustively inspected.

rejected_leads.lead: DOM style handling scans only ele.getFirstChild()
rejected_leads.reason: Potentially leaves additional style text siblings unscanned, but no source-evidenced NekoHTML input path producing multiple actionable style children was established; not strong enough to submit.

Clearly suspicious for ordinary mixed-valid input, but the demonstrated consequence is parser failure/DoS rather than a concrete XSS or other high-impact bypass; rejected as weaker than the SSRF lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Policy <include> destination can escape the documented local-file restriction
rejected_leads.reason: The include href is part of trusted policy configuration; an attacker who controls policy contents can already alter sanitizer rules, so no attacker trust boundary or runtime path was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Dynamic attribute policy strips a character from the configured prefix
rejected_leads.reason: The 'data-' prefix becomes 'data', broadening matches, but the matched attribute is still not an event handler and no concrete script-execution consequence was found.

rejected_leads.lead: Inline CSS handler constructor discards the caller's error-message list
rejected_leads.reason: This appears to affect diagnostics only; cleaned CSS is still generated and validated, so no sanitization bypass was shown.

summary: The strongest source-supported lead is an opt-in SSRF path in CSS @import processing: attacker-controlled stylesheet URLs are fetched server-side after only regex scheme validation, with no destination/private-address allowlist. The bundled policies disable stylesheet embedding, so this requires a policy with embedStyleSheets=true.
